_comment: The reference task set for the agent-only benchmark -- Proposal §2.1, NN-1.
§2.1 states the measurement verbatim: "a cold-start coding agent, given only the repository and
a task, must produce a working QQQ service without human intervention. Target: >=90% success on
the reference task set. Tracked in bench/agent-bench." And `R-13` fires when the rate drops
Each task carries a STARTING POINT and a REFERENCE SOLUTION, and the runner asserts BOTH
directions: the verifier must FAIL on the starting point (or the task is already solved and
measures nothing) and PASS on the reference solution (or the task is unsolvable and measures a
broken verifier). That is what makes the set falsifiable without an agent in the loop -- and it
is also how the set is tested, because a task that fails either direction is a defect in the

target._why: §2.1's target, and R-13's trigger. Both are the Proposal's numbers, not this file's.

tasks.statement: Create a Rust project named `app` that serves HTTP requests.
A Rust project named `app` grants the wall clock but never reads it. Remove the capability it does not use, without breaking the build.
A Rust project named `app` grants `http.server`. Produce a build of it that requires no capabilities at all.
